question: Assume today is 2026-10-27. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of cars manufactured in the United Kingdom in September 2026 (total car production for home and export markets, excluding commercial vehicles), as it will be first reported in the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders' (SMMT) monthly UK car manufacturing release.

target.what: Total number of passenger cars manufactured in the United Kingdom during September 2026 for both home and export markets, as first reported in SMMT's monthly UK car manufacturing release; excludes commercial vehicles.
target.publisher: Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: SMMT headline UK car production (passenger cars), total home plus export, produced at UK plants, September 2026 calendar month. This is a production flow, not registrations, sales, shipments, or deliveries; commercial vehicles are excluded. First-reported figures may be provi

candidates.perspective: SMMT monthly release archive and prior-year seasonality
candidates.hypothesis: The September 2026 total is anchored by the same month in earlier years and by the most recent 2026 monthly run-rate: T_Sep2026 is approximately T_Sep2025 times a recent 2026 year-over-year factor times a seasonal/working-day adjustment. Historical SMMT totals and home/export splits provide the central prior; the transfer assumption is that September seasonality and recent momentum are stable except for identified shocks.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT monthly UK car production totals and home/export splits for September 2019-2025 and for January-August 2026 (or latest months before cutoff), including revisions and SMMT commentary on working days, model changes, and shutdowns. Minimum evidence: September 2025 total and either August 2026 or 2026 year-to-date total.
search_hints: SMMT UK car manufacturing September 2025 total production
SMMT UK car output monthly 2026 home export

candidates.perspective: UK automotive plant capacity and September 2026 operating schedules
candidates.hypothesis: Output can be built plant by plant: T is approximately the sum over UK car plants of capacity_i times utilisation_i times operating_days_i divided by period_days, adjusted for model mix and ramp constraints. Plant capacities and announced shutdowns or line changes constrain plausible output and can reveal deviations from trend. The transfer assumption is that published capacities are achievable and utilisation can be inferred from shifts and schedules.
candidates.data_to_find: Plant capacities for major UK car plants (for example Nissan Sunderland, JLR, Toyota Burnaston, Mini Oxford, Bentley Crewe, Rolls-Royce Goodwood, Aston Martin, McLaren) and September 2026 shift patterns, shutdowns, line changes, and model launches. Minimum evidence: capacities and any announced September 2026 shutdowns.
search_hints: UK car plant capacity Nissan Sunderland JLR Toyota 2025

candidates.perspective: News and company disclosures on September 2026 disruptions
candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 output equals the seasonal baseline times one minus lost plant-days divided by available plant-days for measurable disruptions. Supply-chain shortages, cyber incidents, strikes, floods, energy constraints, or model changeovers can shift output away from history. The transfer assumption is that lost days can be weighted by affected plant capacity.
candidates.data_to_find: September 2026 UK car plant closures or halts, supplier shortages, company production statements, and SMMT comments. Minimum evidence: a list of events with dates and affected plants.

candidates.perspective: UK new-car registrations and import penetration
candidates.hypothesis: Home-market production H is not the same as registrations R, but H is approximately R times one minus import share, plus or minus stock changes; total T is approximately H divided by home-production share. September registrations are published early and can constrain the home component. The transfer assumption is that historical import share and home-production share are stable enough for September 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT UK new car registrations for September 2026, import penetration, and SMMT home/export production splits for 2025 and 2026 year-to-date. Minimum evidence: September 2026 registrations and a historical home-production share.
search_hints: SMMT UK new car registrations September 2026
SMMT car production home export share 2026

candidates.perspective: UK car export trade and port vehicle flows
candidates.hypothesis: Export production E is the dominant share s of total production, so T is approximately E divided by s. Monthly UK car exports under HS 8703 or port vehicle throughput for September 2026 can approximate E, with timing and stock adjustments. The transfer assumption is that export production tracks export trade closely over the month and that the SMMT export share is stable.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC UK trade in passenger cars (HS 8703) monthly for September 2026 or latest 2026 months; SMMT export production totals; port vehicle handling at Southampton, Bristol, Immingham, and other vehicle ports. Minimum evidence: an export share and any September 2026 export or port signal.
search_hints: HMRC UK car exports September 2026 HS 8703

candidates.perspective: Published 2026 UK car production forecasts and industry guidance
candidates.hypothesis: An annual 2026 UK car production forecast P_2026 times the historical September share of annual production, adjusted using 2026 year-to-date actuals, gives an independent prior for September 2026. Forecasts and guidance are intentions, not realisations, so they should be reconciled with SMMT year-to-date data.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT 2026 UK car production outlook, forecasts from Auto Analysis, S&P Global, or Oxford Economics, manufacturer guidance, and any September 2026 production forecast. Minimum evidence: an annual 2026 forecast and a historical September share or 2026 year-to-date actual.
search_hints: UK car output 2026 forecast Auto Analysis

directions.hypothesis: The largest uncertainty in m1 is how much of the September 2025 JLR cyber-halt loss returns in September 2026; plant-level JLR production or SMMT commentary on recovery would calibrate a1/a2 and resolve disagreement between recovery and trend routes.
directions.data_to_find: JLR UK production volumes or plant operating schedules for September 2025 and September 2026, especially Solihull, Halewood and Castle Bromwich; any SMMT statement on cyber-attack recovery.

p29.role: UK total passenger-car production in September 2025, monthly count, known to be depressed by the JLR cyber halt

p90.role: JLR UK annual car output in 2024, used as the pre-halt JLR UK production-rate proxy

p206.role: duration in weeks of the JLR UK factory production halt starting 1 September 2025

a1.role: fraction of the JLR annual-output-derived five-week loss that matches the observed September 2025 shortfall and is recovered by September 2026

a2.role: underlying 2026 versus normalized 2025 UK car output trend factor

methods.rationale: Starts from the observed September 2025 total and adds back an estimate of the JLR output lost to the 2025 cyber halt, then applies a small underlying 2026 trend adjustment. Main dependencies: p29 and p78 are same-source SMMT history; p90 is 2024 JLR output, not 2025 actual; p206 spans into October, so a1 absorbs partial-month and capacity differences. Failure mode is a permanent JLR capacity reduction or a new September 2026 stoppage.

p78.role: UK total passenger-car production in September 2024, normal pre-JLR September baseline

a3.role: September 2026 trend factor relative to the September 2024 baseline

methods.rationale: Uses September 2024, a pre-cyber-attack September, as the normal seasonal baseline and applies a trend factor for 2025 weakness plus partial 2026 recovery. This route avoids p29 as the base, so it is an alternative to m1 rather than a restatement. Main dependency is that 2024 September was not itself abnormal. Failure mode is a structural decline or permanent plant loss since 2024.

p427.role: UK passenger-car production in 2025, annual total

a4.role: September 2026 production index relative to the 2025 average month

methods.rationale: Builds a September 2026 estimate from the 2025 annual car-production level, converts it to an average month, and applies a September seasonal/recovery index. This uses annual output evidence rather than the September 2025 shock level. Main dependency is that the 2025 annual level and a normal September seasonal shape bracket 2026. Failure mode is a large 2026 annual run-rate shift or a September-specific plant schedule different from normal.

assumptions.name: Recovered share of JLR September 2025 shortfall
assumptions.rationale: p90 gives JLR UK 2024 annual output; p206 gives a five-week JLR UK halt from 1 September 2025. The gap between p78 and p29 is close to three-quarters of p90 scaled by p206/k_weeks_per_year, so a1 calibrates the capacity-derived loss to the observed September total shortfall and its assumed recovery. Range allows for 2025 JLR output differing from 2024 and for the halt spilling into October.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has no repeat JLR-wide halt and the lost September 2025 output is largely recovered.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that JLR UK capacity/output was permanently reduced, or that September 2026 has new plant stoppages.

assumptions.name: Underlying 2026 vs normalized 2025 UK car output trend
assumptions.rationale: p61 shows January-August 2026 passenger-car production down 3.9% on 2025, and recent monthly output remains weak. After removing the one-off JLR halt, September 2026 underlying output is assumed slightly below the normalized September 2025 level. Range allows flat-to-weak recovery.
assumptions.applies_when: 2026 demand and plant utilisation remain near the January-August run-rate and no new broad shock occurs.
assumptions.falsified_by: Clear September 2026 recovery well beyond the JLR base effect, or evidence of new supply-chain or plant disruptions.

assumptions.name: September 2026 factor relative to September 2024 baseline
assumptions.rationale: p78 is a pre-JLR normal September baseline. p429 shows 2025 annual car output fell 8.0% from 2024 and p61 shows 2026 January-August car output down 3.9% on 2025, but September 2026 should partly recover from the depressed p29 base. A factor near 0.94 is used rather than applying both declines fully.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2024 is a usable normal September baseline and September 2026 has no major new disruption.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of permanent UK capacity loss after 2024, or a new September 2026 stoppage.

assumptions.name: September 2026 index relative to 2025 average month
assumptions.rationale: p427 is the 2025 annual car total, so dividing by k_months_per_year gives an average 2025 month. p29/p427 makes September 2025 an unusually depressed month, while p78/p85 makes September 2024 a normal high seasonal month. Because September 2026 should recover from the JLR-hit base but remains subject to weak 2026 year-to-date output, an index just above 1 is used.
assumptions.applies_when: 2026 September seasonality is broadly normal in shape and the JLR base effect is the main reason September 2025 was low.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 plant schedules are unusually low or unusually high relative to normal seasonality.

assessment.note: All report the same SMMT August 2026 passenger-car release: 39,328 cars, +6.1% year on year. They are syndicated copies of one underlying measurement, not independent confirmations. p101/p1 are canonical; many are redundant copies.

July 2026 car production 61,767 and June 2026 68,200 come from the same SMMT/statistical series and are duplicated across aggregators. p391 gives the SMMT July release; p65/p541/p848 separately say July was -10.6% year on year.

September 2025 passenger-car production was 51,090, down 27.1%, with 12,269 home and 38,821 export cars; September 2024 was 70,039. p29/p77/p697/p698 are duplicates. The severe September 2025 fall is explained by the JLR halt evidence.

JLR stopped UK factory production for five weeks from 1 September 2025, with a phased restart beginning 8 October 2025. This directly explains why September 2025 is an abnormally low base for September 2026.

p90 gives JLR UK 2024 output 257,110. p762 shows Q3 2026 JLR wholesale volumes rose to 82,400 from 66,165, while p763 shows retail sales fell to 79,000 from 85,371. Wholesale recovery supports production, but JLR wholesale is global and not the same as UK car production; retail weakness does not directly constrain September output.

UK passenger-car production for January-August 2026 was 472,851, down 3.9% on the same period of 2025. The 3.9 is stored as a positive magnitude of a decline, not as a negative signed change; methods must use (1 - p61).
UK car production in 2025 was 717,371, down 8.0% from 2024. The 8.0 is stored as a positive magnitude of a fall; methods must use (1 - p429), not (1 + p429).
UK car production in 2024 was 779,584, and September 2024 was 70,039. p86 is a rounded duplicate of p85; p78 is the useful normal pre-halt September baseline.

September 2026 UK new-car registrations were about 350,5k, up about 12% year on year. This is a demand/registration measure and is not a production total; it can contextualise home demand but cannot be substituted directly for SMMT output.
August 2026 car output was +6.1% year on year, while July was -10.6%. Commentary notes summer-shutdown timing added volatility, so neither month is a clean underlying trend signal by itself.

These carry period fields around September 2026 or 2026 year-to-date, but their publication date is 2025-10-24 and their quotes describe September 2025 or the 2025 year to date. They are misperioded duplicates and must not enter a September 2026 series.
Retrospective September 2025 figures, duplicating p29/p30/p34-p37. p699 is a historical forecast for September 2025, not a September 2026 observation.

Investment, jobs, policy targets, tariff-cost estimates, trade values, plant trivia, and unrelated aerospace/defence items. They do not measure September 2026 UK passenger-car production; some are useful only as background, not as numeric inputs.

p29.role: UK total passenger-car production in September 2025 in cars per month; because JLR UK plants were halted for the whole month, it serves as the non-JLR/base September 2025 output.

a2.role: dimensionless 2026-vs-2025 trend factor for the non-JLR/base component of UK car production.

p90.role: JLR UK annual car output in 2024 in cars per year, used as the annual-rate proxy for JLR's lost September 2025 production and 2026 recovery.

p206.role: duration in weeks of the JLR UK production halt beginning 1 September 2025, used with k_weeks_per_year to convert JLR annual output into a five-week-equivalent volume.

a1.role: dimensionless fraction of the annual-average-derived five-week JLR volume that represents JLR's September 2026 UK output.

methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 JLR recovery route but separates the trend on the non-JLR base from the JLR recovery term. September 2025 p29 is treated as a non-JLR base because the five-week JLR halt from p206/p746 ran through the whole month. JLR's September 2026 contribution is proxied by p90 times the five-week fraction of the year, scaled by a1; p762 supports a JLR recovery but is global wholesale and is not used directly. Main failure modes: p29 may include small JLR output after restart timing, and JLR's 2026 UK rate may differ materially from its 2024 annual average.

p78.role: UK total passenger-car production in September 2024 in cars per month, a normal pre-JLR-halt September baseline.

p429.role: 2025 UK car production change versus 2024, stored as the positive magnitude 8 for an 8.0% fall; used as (1 - p429).

p61.role: 2026 January-August UK car production change versus the same period of 2025, stored as the positive magnitude 3.9 for a 3.9% fall; used as (1 - p61).

a3.role: dimensionless uplift for the fact that the 2025 annual decline includes the five-week JLR halt, which depressed September 2025 disproportionately; it adjusts the mechanically chained 2024-2026 baseline to a normal September 2026.

methods.rationale: Uses September 2024 p78 as a normal September baseline and chains it through the 2025 annual car-production decline p429 and the 2026 January-August car-production decline p61. Both decline points are positive magnitudes, so the formula subtracts them. a3 corrects for the JLR halt being embedded in the 2025 annual decline and for normal September seasonality. This route shares SMMT history with m1 but is not independent of the same underlying production series; it will fail if the 2025 annual decline is not representative of September or if September 2026 breaks from the 2026 year-to-date trend.

p427.role: UK passenger-car production in 2025 in cars per year, annual total used to form the 2025 average monthly output base.

a4.role: dimensionless September 2026 production index relative to the 2025 average month, combining normal September seasonality and the 2026 trend/JLR recovery.

methods.rationale: Simple run-rate route: take the 2025 annual car-production total p427, divide by twelve, and apply a September 2026 index a4. The index is anchored on the 2024 September seasonal factor from p78/p85 and the 2026 year-to-date decline p61, with an upward allowance for JLR recovery. It is useful as an independent structural check against the JLR add-back route, but it will fail if the 2025 annual average is distorted by the September-October 2025 halt or if September seasonality changes.

assumptions.name: JLR September 2026 output as fraction of annual-rate five-week proxy
assumptions.rationale: p90 gives JLR UK 2024 output 257,110/year, so a five-week annual-average proxy is about 24.7k cars. September 2025 was 51,090 versus September 2024 70,039, and the 2025 annual trend was -8.0%, implying the actual September 2025 JLR loss may have been nearer 13-20k because JLR output was already below its 2024 rate. p762 shows Q3 2026 JLR wholesale volumes recovering strongly to 82,400 from 66,165, but that is global wholesale, not UK production. A factor around 0.8 is therefore appropriate, with a wide range for JLR ramp uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 JLR UK production has substantially resumed and can be proxied from JLR's 2024 UK annual output scaled to a five-week-equivalent volume, with p762 used only as directional recovery evidence.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that JLR UK plants were again halted for part or all of September 2026, or that JLR UK output remained far below its 2024 rate because of model changeover or restructuring.

assumptions.name: Non-JLR 2026 vs 2025 trend factor for September car production
assumptions.rationale: p61 shows January-August 2026 passenger-car output down 3.9% on 2025, while p2 shows August +6.1% but commentary attributes part of that to summer-shutdown timing. A small decline for the non-JLR base is therefore more credible than the August bounce; 0.97 is close to the YTD decline and allows for modest improvement.
assumptions.applies_when: The non-JLR component of UK car production continues near its 2026 year-to-date trend rather than reverting to the noisy August year-on-year rate.
assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 SMMT commentary or plant-level evidence showing a broad non-JLR recovery well above 2025 levels, or a new shutdown at a major non-JLR plant.

assumptions.name: Uplift for JLR halt embedded in the 2025 annual decline
assumptions.rationale: p78 is a normal September 2024 baseline; p429 applies the 2025 full-year decline, but that decline includes the five-week JLR halt from p206/p746, which depressed September 2025 disproportionately. p61 then applies the 2026 January-August decline. Because a uniform annual decline understates a normal September when the halt hit that month entirely, a modest uplift is needed. p762 supports JLR recovery by Q3 2026.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2025 annual decline is used as a trend proxy but September 2025 was disproportionately depressed by the JLR cyber halt, so a normal September 2026 baseline should be somewhat above the mechanically chained 2024-2026 product.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the 2025 annual decline was mostly driven by non-September factors and that September 2025 was already close to the 2025 trend, or that JLR did not recover by September 2026.

assumptions.name: September 2026 index relative to the 2025 average month
assumptions.rationale: p427 gives a 2025 average month of about 59.8k cars. September is seasonally strong: p78/p85 imply September 2024 was about 1.08 times the 2024 average month. Against this, p61 shows 2026 January-August car output down 3.9%, but September 2026 should benefit from JLR recovery absent in September 2025. A net index around 1.10 is consistent with normal September seasonality plus partial recovery, with a range covering both a flat and a stronger rebound.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 behaves like a normal September seasonally and the 2025 annual average is a usable base despite the September-October 2025 JLR disruption.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of abnormal September 2026 shutdowns, model-change losses, or a JLR recovery much weaker or stronger than the Q3 2026 wholesale signal implies.

methods.label: m1

p29.role: UK total passenger-car production in September 2025 in cars per month; because JLR UK plants were halted for the whole month, it serves as the non-JLR/base September 2025 output.

a2.role: dimensionless 2026-vs-2025 trend factor for the non-JLR/base component of UK car production.

p90.role: JLR UK annual car output in 2024 in cars per year, used as the annual-rate proxy for JLR's lost September 2025 production and 2026 recovery.

p206.role: duration in weeks of the JLR UK production halt beginning 1 September 2025, used with k_weeks_per_year to convert JLR annual output into a five-week-equivalent volume.

a1.role: dimensionless fraction of the annual-average-derived five-week JLR volume that represents JLR's September 2026 UK output.

methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 JLR recovery route but separates the trend on the non-JLR base from the JLR recovery term. September 2025 p29 is treated as a non-JLR base because the five-week JLR halt from p206/p746 ran through the whole month. methods.label: m2

p78.role: UK total passenger-car production in September 2024 in cars per month, a normal pre-JLR-halt September baseline.

p429.role: 2025 UK car production change versus 2024, stored as the positive magnitude 8 for an 8.0% fall; used as (1 - p429).

p61.role: 2026 January-August UK car production change versus the same period of 2025, stored as the positive magnitude 3.9 for a 3.9% fall; used as (1 - p61).

a3.role: dimensionless uplift for the fact that the 2025 annual decline includes the five-week JLR halt, which depressed September 2025 disproportionately; it adjusts the mechanically chained 2024-2026 baseline to a normal September 2026.

methods.rationale: Uses September 2024 p78 as a normal September baseline and chains it through the 2025 annual car-production decline p429 and the 2026 January-August car-production decline p61. Both decline points are positive magnitudes, so the formula subtracts them. a3 corrects for the JLR halt being embedded in the 2025 annual decline and for normal September seasonality. This route shares SMMT history with m1

p427.role: UK passenger-car production in 2025 in cars per year, annual total used to form the 2025 average monthly output base.

a4.role: dimensionless September 2026 production index relative to the 2025 average month, combining normal September seasonality and the 2026 trend/JLR recovery.

methods.rationale: Simple run-rate route: take the 2025 annual car-production total p427, divide by twelve, and apply a September 2026 index a4. kept.rationale: p90 gives JLR UK 2024 output 257,110/year, so a five-week annual-average proxy is about 24.7k cars. September 2025 was 51,090 versus September 2024 70,039, and the 2025 annual trend was -8.0%, implying the actual September 2025 JLR loss may have been nearer 13-20k because JLR output was already belo

kept.falsified_by: Evidence that JLR UK plants were again halted for part or all of September 2026, or that JLR UK output remained far below its 2024 rate because of model changeover or restructuring.

kept.name: Uplift for JLR halt embedded in the 2025 annual decline
kept.rationale: p78 is a normal September 2024 baseline; p429 applies the 2025 full-year decline, but that decline includes the five-week JLR halt from p206/p746, which depressed September 2025 disproportionately. p61 then applies the 2026 January-August decline. Because a uniform annual decline understates a norma

kept.falsified_by: Evidence that the 2025 annual decline was mostly driven by non-September factors and that September 2025 was already close to the 2025 trend, or that JLR did not recover by September 2026.

kept.name: September 2026 index relative to the 2025 average month
kept.rationale: p427 gives a 2025 average month of about 59.8k cars. September is seasonally strong: p78/p85 imply September 2024 was about 1.08 times the 2024 average month. Against this, p61 shows 2026 January-August car output down 3.9%, but September 2026 should benefit from JLR recovery absent in September 202

The best estimate for total UK passenger-car production in September 2026 (home plus export, excluding commercial vehicles) is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

Evidence: September 2025 output was [[p29_value]], depressed by the JLR cyberattack halt of [[p206_value]]. September 2024 was [[p78_value]]; 2025 annual output was [[p427_value]], down [[p429_value]], and January–August 2026 was down [[p61_value]]. JLR's 2024 UK output was [[p90_value]].

Three routes were combined by equal weight per block, with the median taken: m1 [[m1_estimate]] (weight [[m1_weight]]), m2 [[m2_estimate]] (weight [[m2_weight]]), m3 [[m3_estimate]] (weight [[m3_weight]]). All depend on analyst assumptions a1–a4 ([[a1_value]], [[a2_value]], [[a3_value]], [[a4_value]]) for JLR recovery and seasonality; these are transfers, not observations.

Main risk: the JLR recovery magnitude is uncertain. Better evidence would be JLR's own monthly UK production or SMMT plant-level data for September 2026.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 JLR September 2026 output as fraction of annual-rate five-week proxy: [[a1_value]] [n], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that JLR UK plants were again halted for part or all of September 2026, or that JLR UK output remained far below its 2024 rate because of model changeover or restructuring.
- a2 Non-JLR 2026 vs 2025 trend factor for September car production: [[a2_value]] [n], range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: September 2026 SMMT commentary or plant-level evidence showing a broad non-JLR recovery well above 2025 levels, or a new shutdown at a major non-JLR plant.
- a3 Uplift for JLR halt embedded in the 2025 annual decline: [[a3_value]] [n], range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that the 2025 annual decline was mostly driven by non-September factors and that September 2025 was already close to the 2025 trend, or that JLR did not recover by September 2026.
- a4 September 2026 index relative to the 2025 average month: [[a4_value]] [n], range [[a4_low]] to [[a4_high]] (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: Evidence of abnormal September 2026 shutdowns, model-change losses, or a JLR recovery much weaker or stronger than the Q3 2026 wholesale signal implies.

final.text:
The best estimate for total UK passenger-car production in September 2026 (home plus export, excluding commercial vehicles) is 65,782 car (80% model-based interval 45,425 to 95,260 car).

Evidence: September 2025 output was 51,090 cars, depressed by the JLR cyberattack halt of 5 weeks. September 2024 was 70,039 car; 2025 annual output was 717,371 car, down 8%, and January–August 2026 was down 3.9%. JLR's 2024 UK output was 257,110 car.

Three routes were combined by equal weight per block, with the median taken: m1 69,727 (weight 0%), m2 65,782 (weight 100%), m3 65,219 (weight 0%). All depend on analyst assumptions a1–a4 (0.8, 0.97, 1.06, 1.1) for JLR recovery and seasonality; these are transfers, not observations.

Main risk: the JLR recovery magnitude is uncertain. Better evidence would be JLR's own monthly UK production or SMMT plant-level data for September 2026.

Unit of the estimate: car (cars manufactured; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 JLR September 2026 output as fraction of annual-rate five-week proxy: 0.8 [n], range 0.5612 to 1.122 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that JLR UK plants were again halted for part or all of September 2026, or that JLR UK output remained far below its 2024 rate because of model changeover or restructuring.
- a2 Non-JLR 2026 vs 2025 trend factor for September car production: 0.97 [n], range 0.8612 to 1.076 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: September 2026 SMMT commentary or plant-level evidence showing a broad non-JLR recovery well above 2025 levels, or a new shutdown at a major non-JLR plant.
- a3 Uplift for JLR halt embedded in the 2025 annual decline: 1.06 [n], range 0.7526 to 1.505 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that the 2025 annual decline was mostly driven by non-September factors and that September 2025 was already close to the 2025 trend, or that JLR did not recover by September 2026.
- a4 September 2026 index relative to the 2025 average month: 1.1 [n], range 0.7732 to 1.546 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: Evidence of abnormal September 2026 shutdowns, model-change losses, or a JLR recovery much weaker or stronger than the Q3 2026 wholesale signal implies.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p29 * a2 + p90 * (p206 / k_weeks_per_year) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 57,343 to 85,323; result unit car converted to car; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p78 * (1 - p429) * (1 - p61) * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 44,187 to 97,516; result unit (car/month) * 1 month converted to car; own 80% width x/÷1.49 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p427 / k_months_per_year * a4; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 44,339 to 96,702; result unit (car/month) * 1 month converted to car; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 3 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 69,727 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: 65,782 (width x/÷1.49, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B3 = m3: 65,219 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.45; Birge ratio 0.13 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.45.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
